cards.title: List customer names
cards.explanation: Choose explicit columns and stable output names. All shared SQL cards run on the seeded SQLite and PostgreSQL playgrounds.

cards.title: Find paid orders over a threshold
cards.explanation: Filter before aggregation. Numeric amounts use integer units in this fixture to avoid floating-point rounding.

cards.title: Find the two largest orders
cards.explanation: The id tie breaker makes the limited result deterministic.

cards.title: Join customers to their orders
cards.code:
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.total
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY o.id;
cards.explanation: Each order becomes one result row with its customer name.

cards.title: Find customers without orders
cards.code:
SELECT c.id, c.name
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL
ORDER BY c.id;
cards.explanation: The missing non-null primary key identifies customers with no matching order.

cards.title: Group paid totals per customer
cards.code:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS paid_total
FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(total) >= 50
ORDER BY customer_id;
cards.explanation: Aggregate only paid orders and keep customers reaching the threshold.

cards.title: Find customers with no email
cards.explanation: NULL represents an absent value. It differs from an empty string. Default NULL sort position differs between SQLite and PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Find customers with a paid order
cards.explanation: EXISTS returns each customer once even when several paid orders match.

cards.title: Name customer totals before filtering
cards.explanation: Use a CTE to separate aggregation from the final report.

cards.title: Rank orders within each customer
cards.explanation: Number each customer’s orders from largest to smallest with a stable tie breaker.

cards.title: Add a customer with a supplied key
cards.code:
INSERT INTO customers (id, name, email)
VALUES (5, 'Eve', 'eve@example.test');
cards.explanation: Shared examples supply ids explicitly: generated-key syntax differs between SQLite and PostgreSQL.

cards.title: Mark one order as paid
cards.code:
UPDATE orders SET status = 'paid'
WHERE id = 2 AND status = 'pending';
cards.explanation: The key and current-state predicate prevent changing unrelated orders.

cards.title: Delete one cancelled order
cards.code:
DELETE FROM orders
WHERE id = 4 AND status = 'cancelled';
cards.explanation: Delete only the known cancelled order; the seeded customer remains.

cards.title: Enforce unique inventory codes
cards.explanation: Duplicate codes, missing codes and negative quantities are rejected by both engines.

cards.title: Index customer order lookups
cards.code:
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_total
ON orders (customer_id, total);
cards.explanation: This index supports filtering orders by customer and then by total. Plans are engine-specific.

cards.title: Roll back a trial price change
cards.explanation: The trial update is discarded. The database tests also provoke a constraint error and recover through a savepoint on both engines.

cards.title: Bind a customer lookup value (SQLite)
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = ?;
cards.explanation: SQLite only. Bind [1] through the SQLite API. The Python sqlite3 companion uses this exact convention. Use the PostgreSQL variant after changing the dialect.

cards.title: Enable SQLite foreign-key enforcement
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
cards.explanation: SQLite only. This is connection-local and must run outside an active transaction.

cards.title: Return a generated PostgreSQL key
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. No SQLite rowid assumptions are used.

cards.title: Update a customer on a key conflict
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
INSERT INTO customers (id, name, email)
VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.test')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name
RETURNING id, name;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. The existing email remains unchanged because only name is assigned.

cards.title: Read a PostgreSQL JSON property
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT payload::jsonb->>'name' AS name FROM documents
WHERE CASE WHEN id < 4 THEN payload::jsonb @> '{"name":"Ada"}'::jsonb ELSE FALSE END
ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL 18.4. The documents seed provides valid objects at ids 1–3 and malformed text at id 4. CASE guards the fixture cast before containment; a plain AND does not promise evaluation order. Real ingestion must validate JSON before JSONB storage.

cards.title: Bind a customer lookup value (PostgreSQL)
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id = $1;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL only. Pass [1] as the values array to node-postgres, or pass 1 to Go QueryRowContext. Values never become SQL syntax.

cards.title: List the distinct order states
cards.code: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orders ORDER BY status;
cards.explanation: Build a filter menu without repeating states. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Count known unique contacts and missing contacts
cards.code: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT email), COUNT(*) - COUNT(email) FROM customers;
cards.explanation: NULL contacts do not count as known addresses; count missing separately. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Combine paid and pending audiences without duplicates
cards.code:
SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
UNION SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY customer_id;
cards.explanation: Ada appears in both audiences but must receive one message. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Find customers with both paid and pending orders
cards.code:
SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY customer_id;
cards.explanation: Intersect the two eligibility sets rather than joining duplicate order rows. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Find customers without a paid order
cards.code:
SELECT id FROM customers
EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: Subtract paid customers, including customers with no orders. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Preserve duplicate events from two feeds
cards.code:
SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
UNION ALL SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY customer_id;
cards.explanation: A feed represents events, so the same customer may occur twice. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Label missing and empty contacts differently
cards.code:
SELECT id, CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN email = '' THEN 'empty' ELSE 'known' END AS state
FROM customers ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: A blank address is distinct from absent data. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Compute the paid share without dividing by zero
cards.code: SELECT COALESCE(CAST(1 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'paid' THEN total ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(total), 0), 0.0) AS paid_share FROM orders;
cards.explanation: Return zero when there is no billed amount; multiply by 1.0 for fractional division. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Show employees even when they lack managers
cards.code:
SELECT e.id, e.name, COALESCE(m.name, 'unassigned') AS manager
FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id ORDER BY e.id;
cards.explanation: The self join preserves the root and uses aliases to separate roles. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Avoid inflating revenue when joining multiple children
cards.code:
WITH revenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id)
SELECT c.id, COALESCE(r.total, 0) AS total, COUNT(o.id) AS orders
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN revenue r ON r.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, r.total ORDER BY c.id;
cards.explanation: Revenue is calculated before joining orders again, preserving the one-row-per-customer total. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Continue a descending amount page with ties
cards.explanation: The previous page ended at (total=50, id=3); continue using both sort components. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Read a stable second page in a fixed snapshot
cards.code: SELECT id, total FROM orders ORDER BY total DESC, id ASC LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2;
cards.explanation: Suitable for a small fixed dataset; live changes can shift offsets. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Report paid totals alongside every customer
cards.explanation: Filtered child-key counts avoid treating the null-extended join row as an order. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Keep customers with multiple orders and a paid order
cards.explanation: HAVING applies after independent filtered and unfiltered counts. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Compare competition ranking with dense ranking
cards.explanation: Rank on amount alone so equal amounts tie; the outer id orders tied output. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Compare peer-inclusive totals with row-by-row totals
cards.explanation: RANGE includes every equal-amount peer; ROWS uses the unique id tie-breaker. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Carry the final order amount across a partition
cards.explanation: An explicit complete frame avoids LAST_VALUE returning only the current row value. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Traverse a manager tree with a finite depth budget
cards.explanation: Includes the root and limits traversal depth even if bad source data contains a cycle. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Follow one employee toward their reporting root
cards.explanation: Walk upwards using the manager key; missing starting employees produce an empty report. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Add a defaulted status without losing existing customers
cards.explanation: A constant non-null default supplies values for existing and future rows. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Rename a disposable contact column atomically
cards.explanation: Update application queries in the same migration plan; old names stop working. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Keep the required update while discarding an optional one
cards.explanation: The first update commits and the optional adjustment disappears. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Show why releasing a savepoint does not commit
cards.explanation: The outer rollback still undoes released inner work. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Merge a repeated customer import by primary key
cards.explanation: Only a primary-key conflict updates the existing name; other constraints still apply. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Skip duplicate import keys without replacing records
cards.explanation: A repeated key preserves the existing customer; no delete-and-reinsert behavior. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Reserve a writer before adjusting a balance
cards.explanation: Acquire the reservation before dependent reads; the caller handles busy errors with bounded whole-transaction retries. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Reject a stale amount with an optimistic predicate
cards.explanation: Read changes() immediately after UPDATE; zero means missing/stale and the caller must refresh. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Read a consistent paid report in Repeatable Read
cards.explanation: The runner preserves the last row-producing result; copied SQL clients show SELECT before COMMIT. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; PostgreSQL 18.4.

cards.title: Increment on the server instead of overwriting a stale value
cards.explanation: Read Committed updates the current row after any conflicting writer completes; multi-row invariants may need stronger isolation. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; PostgreSQL 18.4.

cards.title: Extract names while tolerating malformed imported JSON
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT id, CASE WHEN json_valid(payload) THEN json_extract(payload, '$.name') ELSE 'invalid' END AS name FROM documents ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: CASE guards the extraction; malformed documents get an explicit fallback. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Distinguish absent JSON keys from explicit null
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT id, CASE WHEN json_valid(payload) THEN COALESCE(json_type(payload, '$.name'), 'missing') ELSE 'invalid' END AS kind FROM documents ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: json_type returns text null for JSON null and SQL NULL for an absent key. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Normalize imported offsets to a UTC report day
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT id, datetime(occurred_at) AS utc FROM events ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: The seed includes equivalent offset instants and one invalid timestamp, which yields NULL. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Count a half-open UTC day across input offsets
cards.code:
-- SQLite only
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE datetime(occurred_at) >= '2026-10-17 00:00:00' AND datetime(occurred_at) < '2026-10-18 00:00:00';
cards.explanation: Normalize before comparing; midnight at the upper boundary belongs to the next day. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1.

cards.title: Format offset instants with an explicit reporting zone
cards.explanation: This curated input excludes the invalid row; real ingestion must reject invalid text before storing timestamptz. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; PostgreSQL 18.4.

cards.title: Count instants in an explicit UTC day
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events
WHERE CASE WHEN id < 4 THEN occurred_at::timestamptz END >= '2026-10-17T00:00:00Z'::timestamptz
AND CASE WHEN id < 4 THEN occurred_at::timestamptz END < '2026-10-18T00:00:00Z'::timestamptz;
cards.explanation: An offset-aware interval excludes the next midnight; use a zone-defined calendar boundary for non-UTC business days. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; PostgreSQL 18.4.

cards.title: Separate missing JSONB keys from JSON null
cards.explanation: The valid-input fixture distinguishes JSON null from an absent key; malformed text must be rejected at ingestion. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; PostgreSQL 18.4.

cards.title: Patch a JSONB property without deleting unrelated fields
cards.code:
-- PostgreSQL only
SELECT id, jsonb_set(payload::jsonb, '{active}', 'true'::jsonb)->>'name' AS name,
 jsonb_set(payload::jsonb, '{active}', 'true'::jsonb)->>'active' AS active
FROM documents WHERE id < 4 ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL 18.4. The documents seed has three valid object payloads before malformed row 4. Patch active while preserving name, including null or missing names. Invalid JSON must be rejected at ingestion.

cards.title: Index only paid orders for a focused lookup
cards.code:
CREATE INDEX paid_customer ON orders (customer_id, total) WHERE status = 'paid';
SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' AND customer_id = 1 ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: The query predicate matches the partial-index condition; tiny tables may still favor a scan. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Index a normalized customer name expression
cards.code:
CREATE INDEX customer_lower_name ON customers (lower(name));
SELECT id FROM customers WHERE lower(name) = 'ada' ORDER BY id;
cards.explanation: Use the same immutable/built-in expression in the lookup; this is simple ASCII folding, not locale-aware identity. Uses the disposable SQL playground seed; SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. No client imports required.

cards.title: Find customers with no paid orders using NOT EXISTS
cards.code:
SELECT c.id, c.name FROM customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid') ORDER BY c.id;
cards.explanation: SQLite 3.53.1 / PostgreSQL 18.4. Correlate to each customer and reject any paid match; cancelled-only and no-order customers remain. NOT EXISTS avoids the NULL contamination of NOT IN.

cards.title: Prepare and reuse a typed PostgreSQL lookup
cards.explanation: PostgreSQL 18.4. SQL PREPARE declares a session-scoped integer parameter and EXECUTE supplies its value. DEALLOCATE releases the named statement. Host-driver binding remains a separate API; do not interpolate user input into EXECUTE text.
